patch_description:
This approach learns the QUBO from deterministic routing experiments instead of assigning two-hop rewards.

It explores valid networks using degree-preserving exchanges, evaluating them with shortest-path flow splitting followed by congestion-priced routing. A regularized regression then distills these approximate congestion scores into link costs and outgoing/incoming neighbor-pair costs. A modest elite-network prior steers samples toward promising regions without fixing one topology.

The model captures multihop congestion indirectly through its training labels. It uses fewer than n³ quadratic terms, predominantly within the same neighbor groups already coupled by the degree constraints. No LP solver or external optimization library is used.
